Acting by himself (as Circuit Justice for the Eighth Circuit), Justice Kavanaugh has *denied* Missouri's (fairly ridiculous) emergency application asking #SCOTUS to put back into effect its 2026 gerrymander.

The Missouri Supreme Court's ruling that reverted back to the 2022 map will stand.

After going 4.5 months without filing a single emergency application, this is now the *fifth* emergency request the federal government has brought to the Court in the last six weeks (and we're about to match the *total* number of applications filed during the entire first Trump administration).

“Having a uniform and predictable set of legislatively imposed rules to govern the release of their papers going forward would not only help to increase the Court’s transparency, but it would also reaffirm that the justices’ work, which increasingly *affects* all of us, also *belongs* to all of us.”

As I explained the last time this dumb argument made the rounds, if Congress was never allowed to change the Court’s size (something it’s done seven times), that would mean four of the *current* justices (all of whom are Republicans) hold unconstitutionally created seats:

www.ms.now/opinion/repu...

In a *different* case, a federal district court has now put the 2026 map back into effect—on a different theory. That ruling *should* be subject to a stay from either the Eighth Circuit or #SCOTUS, because that should be covered by Purcell. But we’re not there yet.
